einzeiler: A couple married to other people and apart for years reexamines their recurring bond.
kurzfassung: Esther Perel counsels a couple who have spent over fifteen years cycling between intense connection and emotional shutdown. The male partner reflects on early financial struggles, the absence of a father figure, and his defensive habit of keeping expectations low to avoid failure. Meanwhile, his partner shares her own vulnerabilities around self-worth and her desire for him to show up fully as a father and boyfriend. Through the session, both partners confront the patterns keeping them distant and ultimately embrace a moment of physical and emotional reconnection.
stichpunkte: The couple met in high school, had a daughter in college, and split up for nearly fifteen years.
During their time apart, both married other people and had children before reconnecting.
The male partner describes a severe period of financial hardship in his early twenties involving housing instability.
He connects his current tendency to shut down emotionally to childhood memories of his mother coming home in a bad mood.
He admits to keeping expectations deliberately low so that he cannot fail or disappoint anyone.
His partner expresses her exhaustion with feeling alone even when they share a home.
She reflects on internalizing societal messages about Black women and the pain of feeling unwanted when he holds back physically.
Esther Perel helps them reframe his withdrawal not as a desire for isolation, but as a survival mechanism.
The session concludes with the couple holding each other and embracing physical closeness.

clips.hook: Living in a very, very dark place
clips.text: The male guest looks back at the severe emotional distress he experienced during his early twenties.

clips.hook: Life was just like a game
clips.text: The male guest admits that he viewed life as a party and never considered what adulthood would actually require of him.

clips.hook: Afraid to give in to that time
clips.text: The male guest struggles to articulate his fear of allowing himself to feel secure and cared for.

clips.hook: The sound of dread in the driveway
clips.text: The male guest describes how hearing his mother's car pull up during his teenage years filled him and his sister with anxiety.

clips.hook: An act of love and a political statement
clips.text: The female guest reflects on the deep cultural and personal importance of commitment and strong family bonds.

beschreibung:
This is a classic session of Where Should We Begin? They've been on and off for almost 20 years. While she takes care of his and their child, she wants to know that he's also there for her. He's been battling depression for years. And the shame that comes with it.

Producer’s Note: When our anonymous guests do a session with Esther for the podcast, it is an act of generosity for everyone who listens. These sessions are meant not only to support the people in the room with Esther, but all of us who learn from their stories. Our stories have many chapters, and what you hear is just one moment in someone’s journey. So even though the sessions are anonymous, please remember that real people are behind them and they may be reading your comments.

Also, please join me on Entre Nous, my new home on Substack for anyone who wants to live, love, and work with more connection and imagination. I invite you to sign up and become a free or paid member at estherperel.substack.com
